# CWE-250: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges — Detection in IaC Scripts

## Overview
In IaC contexts, this weakness manifests when resources, containers, services, or identities are provisioned with broader permissions than operationally required, violating the **Principle of Least Privilege**.

---

## Necessary Weaknesses to Detect

### 1. Over-Privileged Identity and Access Policies
Granting administrative or wildcard permissions to identities that only require narrow, specific access.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `Action: "*"`, `actions: ["*"]` | All actions permitted |
| `Resource: "*"`, `resources: ["*"]` | Access to all resources |
| `Effect: Allow` (without restrictive `Condition`) | Unconditional broad grant |
| `AdministratorAccess`, `FullAccess`, `PowerUser` | Predefined admin policy attachment |
| `NotAction`, `NotResource` | Inverse policies may unintentionally grant excess permissions |
| `policy_arn` referencing admin-level managed policies | Admin policy attachment |
| `inline_policy` with broad allow statements | Embedded over-permissive policy |

---

### 2. Container/Process Running as Root
Services or containers configured to execute as the root user or UID 0.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `runAsUser: 0` | Explicit root UID execution |
| `runAsNonRoot: false` | Non-root not enforced |
| `user: root`, `USER root` | Root user designation |
| Absence of `runAsUser`, `runAsGroup` | Default root execution likely |
| `securityContext: {}` or missing `securityContext` | No security constraints applied |

---

### 3. Privileged Container Execution
Containers granted full host-level capabilities.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `privileged: true` | Container has full host privileges |
| `privileged_containers: true` | Cluster-level privileged mode |
| Absence of `securityContext.privileged: false` | Privilege not explicitly restricted |

---

### 4. Privilege Escalation Permitted
Containers or processes allowed to gain higher privileges than their parent.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true` | Escalation explicitly permitted |
| Absence of `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` | Escalation not restricted |
| `setuid`, `setgid` bits implied by capability additions | Privilege elevation capability |

---

### 5. Excessive Linux Capabilities Added
Adding dangerous kernel capabilities beyond what the workload needs.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `capabilities.add: ["ALL"]` | All capabilities granted |
| `cap_add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]` | Administrative kernel capability |
| `cap_add: ["NET_ADMIN"]`, `["NET_RAW"]` | Network-level privileged operations |
| `cap_add: ["SYS_PTRACE"]` | Process tracing capability |
| Absence of `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]` | No capability minimization |

---

### 6. Over-Privileged Service Accounts and Role Bindings
Binding identities to administrative or cluster-wide roles unnecessarily.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `cluster-admin` in `roleRef` | Highest Kubernetes privilege |
| `ClusterRoleBinding` assigning broad subjects | Cluster-wide permission grant |
| `serviceAccountName: default` | Default account with inherited permissions |
| `automountServiceAccountToken: true` | Auto-mounted token may be over-privileged |
| `verbs: ["*"]` in role rules | All API operations permitted |
| `role: admin`, `role: owner`, `role: editor` at resource level | Elevated role assignment |

---

### 7. Host Namespace and Resource Sharing
Containers accessing host-level namespaces, amplifying the impact of any compromise.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `hostPID: true` | Access to all host processes |
| `hostIPC: true` | Shared interprocess communication |
| `hostNetwork: true` | Access to host network stack |
| `hostPath` volumes (especially `/`, `/etc`, `/var`) | Direct host filesystem access |
| `readOnlyRootFilesystem: false` or absent | Writable root filesystem |

---

### 8. Overly Permissive Network Access Rules
Firewall or security group rules granting unrestricted inbound/outbound access, compounding privilege exposure.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `cidr: 0.0.0.0/0`, `cidr: ::/0` | Unrestricted IP range |
| `from_port: 0`, `to_port: 65535` | All ports open |
| `protocol: -1` or `protocol: all` | All protocols permitted |
| `source: 0.0.0.0/0` in inbound rules | Any source allowed |
| `ingress: []` allowing all, absent egress restrictions | No egress filtering |

---

### 9. Absence of Resource-Level Access Restrictions
Policies that fail to scope permissions to specific resources.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| `resource: "*"` with no path qualifiers | Unscoped resource access |
| Missing `Condition` block in sensitive allow policies | No contextual restriction |
| Absence of `principal` constraints | Policy applies to all identities |
| `scope: global` or `scope: all` without justification | Overly broad scope |

---

### 10. Missing or Disabled Security Context Controls
Lack of explicit security hardening settings that enforce least privilege at runtime.

| Keywords / Attributes / Fields | Implication |
|---|---|
| Absent `seccompProfile` or `Unconfined` setting | No syscall filtering |
| Absent `appArmorProfile` | No AppArmor policy |
| `seLinuxOptions` not configured | SELinux not constraining the process |
| Missing `podSecurityContext` | Pod-level security not defined |
| `drop: []` under capabilities | No capability removal |

---

## Summary Table of Key Signals

| Category | Critical Signal |
|---|---|
| IAM Policy | Wildcard `Action` + `Resource`, admin policy names |
| Container Identity | `runAsUser: 0`, missing `runAsNonRoot` |
| Privileged Mode | `privileged: true` |
| Escalation | `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true` or absent |
| Capabilities | `add: ["ALL"]` or sensitive individual caps |
| RBAC | `cluster-admin` binding, `verbs: ["*"]` |
| Host Access | `hostPID`, `hostNetwork`, `hostPath: /` |
| Network | `0.0.0.0/0` with broad port ranges |
| Scope | `resource: "*"` without conditions |
| Hardening Absent | No `seccomp`, no `appArmor`, no `seLinux` options |

package Cx

import data.generic.ansible as ansLib
import data.generic.common as commonLib

# Playbook-level: running as root via become_user
CxPolicy[result] {
	playbook := input.document[i].playbooks[_]
	ansLib.isAnsibleTrue(playbook.become)
	lower(playbook.become_user) == "root"

	result := {
		"documentId": input.document[i].id,
		"resourceType": "n/a",
		"resourceName": "n/a",
		"searchKey": "become_user",
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'become_user' should not be 'root' to follow the principle of least privilege",
		"keyActualValue": "'become_user' is set to 'root'",
	}
}

# Task-level: running as root via become_user
CxPolicy[result] {
	task := ansLib.tasks[id][_]
	ansLib.isAnsibleTrue(task.become)
	lower(task.become_user) == "root"

	result := {
		"documentId": id,
		"resourceType": "n/a",
		"resourceName": task.name,
		"searchKey": sprintf("name={{%s}}.become_user", [task.name]),
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'become_user' should not be 'root'",
		"keyActualValue": "'become_user' is set to 'root'",
	}
}

# Docker container running in privileged mode
CxPolicy[result] {
	task := ansLib.tasks[id][_]
	docker_mods := {"community.docker.docker_container", "docker_container"}
	module := docker_mods[_]
	container := task[module]
	ansLib.isAnsibleTrue(container.privileged)

	result := {
		"documentId": id,
		"resourceType": module,
		"resourceName": task.name,
		"searchKey": sprintf("name={{%s}}.{{%s}}.privileged", [task.name, module]),
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'privileged' should not be 'true'",
		"keyActualValue": "'privileged' is set to 'true'",
	}
}

# Docker container running as root user (string)
CxPolicy[result] {
	task := ansLib.tasks[id][_]
	docker_mods := {"community.docker.docker_container", "docker_container"}
	module := docker_mods[_]
	container := task[module]
	lower(container.user) == "root"

	result := {
		"documentId": id,
		"resourceType": module,
		"resourceName": task.name,
		"searchKey": sprintf("name={{%s}}.{{%s}}.user", [task.name, module]),
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'user' should not be 'root'",
		"keyActualValue": "'user' is set to 'root'",
	}
}

# Docker container running as UID 0 (integer)
CxPolicy[result] {
	task := ansLib.tasks[id][_]
	docker_mods := {"community.docker.docker_container", "docker_container"}
	module := docker_mods[_]
	container := task[module]
	container.user == 0

	result := {
		"documentId": id,
		"resourceType": module,
		"resourceName": task.name,
		"searchKey": sprintf("name={{%s}}.{{%s}}.user", [task.name, module]),
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'user' should not be '0' (root UID)",
		"keyActualValue": "'user' is set to '0' (root UID)",
	}
}

# Docker container with dangerous Linux capabilities added
CxPolicy[result] {
	task := ansLib.tasks[id][_]
	docker_mods := {"community.docker.docker_container", "docker_container"}
	module := docker_mods[_]
	container := task[module]
	dangerous_caps := {"ALL", "SYS_ADMIN", "NET_ADMIN", "NET_RAW", "SYS_PTRACE"}
	cap := container.cap_add[_]
	upper(cap) == dangerous_caps[_]

	result := {
		"documentId": id,
		"resourceType": module,
		"resourceName": task.name,
		"searchKey": sprintf("name={{%s}}.{{%s}}.cap_add", [task.name, module]),
		"issueType": "IncorrectValue",
		"keyExpectedValue": "'cap_add' should not contain dangerous capabilities (ALL, SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, SYS_PTRACE)",
		"keyActualValue": sprintf("'cap_add' contains dangerous capability '%s'", [cap]),
	}
}
